newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia says to use own chip for CDMA phone.
newsitem.headline: Nokia says to use own chip for CDMA phone.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications group Nokia Oy said on Monday it would use its own purpose designed chips in its Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) cellular phones due for first deliveries this summer.
"Nokia has designed its own CDMA chip se for use in Nokia products scheduled for commercial delivery beginning in the summer of 1997," Nokia said in a statement.

It said it would be the first company to offer "a competitive and alternative CDMA design", adding its first CDMA handsets would have high voice quality and fully support IS-95A features such as short messaging and caller line identification.
It also said the design of its first CDMA phone would be based on its Nokia 2100 series.
